Entrust nShield

Hardware Security Modules providing a FIPS-certified hardware root of trust for cryptographic key management, code signing, and PKI in regulated and high-assurance environments.

Security Cloud Mobility Data Centre

Overview

Entrust nShield Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) are purpose-built cryptographic devices that generate, store, and protect private keys in tamper-resistant hardware. An HSM ensures that cryptographic keys used for TLS certificates, code signing, database encryption, or PKI operations never exist in software – they are generated inside the hardware, never exported in the clear, and all cryptographic operations occur within the device itself. This provides a certified, auditable hardware root of trust that software-based key management cannot offer.

nShield HSMs are deployed in organisations where the compromise of a cryptographic key would represent a critical risk – financial institutions issuing payment credentials, government agencies operating national PKI infrastructure, defence contractors signing firmware, and large enterprises meeting FIPS 140-2 or GDPR data protection requirements. The nShield product line spans network-attached appliances, PCIe cards embedded in servers, and USB-attached devices for smaller deployments. nShield as a Service extends the same capability to cloud environments as a subscription.

Arrow ECS UK's Entrust relationship covers the nShield HSM product line, confirmed through 571 transaction lines in 2025. The portfolio includes hardware appliances, software, support contracts, and Remote Administration Smart Cards for secure HSM management. Arrow's Entrust book spans a wide range of end-user organisations across the UK and Ireland, reflecting the broad applicability of HSM technology across regulated industries.

Scope note: Arrow ECS UK's Entrust relationship covers the nShield HSM product line. Entrust's broader portfolio (identity verification, IAM, certificate services) is available directly from Entrust but is not distributed through Arrow ECS UK.

nShield Connect HSM
Network-attached HSM appliance providing shared cryptographic services to multiple servers and applications simultaneously. Operates as a network device, accessed over an encrypted channel. The most common nShield deployment for enterprise PKI and application key management.
Network-attached FIPS 140-2 L3 Shared key services
nShield Solo (PCIe)
HSM embedded directly in a server as a PCIe card. Provides dedicated, low-latency cryptographic operations for a single host. Used in high-throughput environments such as certificate authority servers, payment processing nodes, and mainframe-adjacent key management.
PCIe embedded Low latency Dedicated
nShield Edge (USB)
Portable, USB-attached HSM for low-volume cryptographic operations or development and test environments. Also used for secure key generation and ceremony use cases where a portable, certified device is required.
USB portable Key ceremony Dev / test
nShield as a Service
Cloud-delivered HSM capability available as a subscription. Provides the same nShield cryptographic services without on-premises hardware – accessed via a dedicated, isolated cloud partition. Suited to organisations with cloud-first strategies or hybrid deployments alongside on-premises HSMs.
Cloud HSM Subscription SaaS
Remote Admin Cards
Smart cards used for secure remote administration of nShield HSMs. Remote Admin Cards allow authorised administrators to manage, configure, and perform key ceremonies on HSMs without physical access – confirmed in Arrow's 2025 sales data as a regularly transacted item.

Cross-sell & Expansion Opportunities

IBM
HSM for IBM Z & LinuxONE Cryptographic Security
IBM Z's built-in Crypto Express processors handle on-board cryptographic operations, but organisations with high-assurance requirements often deploy external HSMs for key escrow, certificate authority operations, and compliance with FIPS 140-2 Level 3 mandates. Entrust nShield HSMs are a confirmed IBM Z security partner technology – any IBM Z security conversation touching PKI, encryption key management, or compliance should include Entrust nShield as a natural expansion.
F5 Networks
Hardware Key Protection for F5 SSL & WAF
F5 BIG-IP handles large volumes of TLS connections – the private keys used to terminate those connections are valuable targets. F5 BIG-IP and SSL Orchestrator support network HSM integration, allowing private keys to be generated and stored in an Entrust nShield HSM rather than in software on the F5 device. This provides FIPS 140-2 Level 3 key protection and simplifies compliance for PCI DSS, DORA, and public sector security requirements. A natural expansion in any F5 SSL Orchestrator or high-availability WAF deployment.
Black Duck
Code Signing After Open-Source Scanning
Black Duck scans software for open-source vulnerabilities and licence risk before it is released. Entrust nShield HSMs protect the code signing keys used to sign the software after it passes inspection. The two sit at adjacent points in the secure software release pipeline: Black Duck ensures the software is clean, Entrust ensures the signature proving its authenticity cannot be forged. Relevant in any organisation running a formal software release process or meeting SBOM and supply chain security requirements.
OPSWAT
PKI Root of Trust for OPSWAT Device Identity
OPSWAT MetaAccess can use certificate-based device identity as part of its compliance checks – verifying that a device holds a valid certificate issued by a trusted CA before granting network access. Entrust nShield HSMs are the hardware root of trust for the PKI infrastructure issuing those certificates. In environments with high-assurance device identity requirements – such as defence or critical infrastructure sites running OPSWAT – the two products form a credible, hardware-backed identity and access chain.

Competitive Landscape

The HSM market is concentrated. You will typically encounter one or two alternatives on each shortlist.

Thales Luna HSM
Hardware Security Modules
Thales Luna is the primary global competitor to Entrust nShield. Both are FIPS 140-2 Level 3 certified, broadly compatible with the same ecosystems, and available as network-attached and PCIe form factors. Thales has broader cloud HSM integrations (AWS CloudHSM Classic, Azure Dedicated HSM). Entrust nShield differentiates on its CodeSafe programmable HSM capability and its long-established partner ecosystem. Many enterprises standardise on one or the other – replacing the incumbent requires strong justification.
Utimaco HSM
Hardware Security Modules
Utimaco competes in the HSM market with its SecurityServer and CryptoServer product lines. Utimaco has particular strength in payment HSMs (PCI-compliant) and German government/public sector. Entrust nShield is more commonly encountered in UK and US enterprise deployments. Utimaco is a less frequent alternative in Arrow's primary market.
AWS / Azure Cloud HSM
Cloud-delivered HSM
AWS CloudHSM and Azure Dedicated HSM provide cloud-native HSM services at a lower total cost for cloud-first workloads. They compete primarily with nShield as a Service. On-premises nShield competes where organisations cannot use cloud HSMs for regulatory or sovereignty reasons, or where they need hardware HSMs co-located with their applications. Hybrid scenarios – on-premises nShield plus cloud HSM – are common in large enterprises.

Ideal Customer Profile

Organisation Size
Mid-market to large enterprise. HSMs are typically bought by organisations with a formal PKI, a certificate authority function, or a compliance mandate requiring hardware key protection. Not a small-business product.
Verticals
Financial services (payment systems, banking PKI), government (national PKI, defence), healthcare, telco, and any organisation subject to FIPS 140-2, PCI DSS, DORA, or NIS2 requirements for cryptographic key management.
Trigger Events
PKI infrastructure project; certificate authority deployment or refresh; compliance audit requiring FIPS 140-2 Level 3; IBM Z encryption project; code signing programme; post-quantum cryptography readiness assessment.
Key Personas
CISO, Head of Cryptography / PKI, Security Architect, Compliance Officer. IBM Z accounts: Head of Infrastructure or Mainframe Architect. Often requires engagement at Head of IT Security or above to proceed.
